summary: Tata Steel's Rs 28,000 cr divestment of its tubes business into a controlling stake in APL Apollo reshapes the domestic steel-pipe value chain just as the EU slaps a fresh anti-dumping duty on Indian flat steel; SEBI's FPI-disclosure rollback and its still-undecided MTF free-float cap cut in opposite directions for capital-markets infrastructure stocks. Decided policy moves — Andhra's SMR nuclear clearance, the EV-charging platform's national expansion, a tightened pre-NELP profit-share regime alongside a 150-well drilling program, and new UK/NZ tariff schedules on Scotch and wine — keep repricing capex, energy and consumer-staples exposures even though none of this week's news named a universe company directly.

drivers.what: Tata Steel board approves selling tubes/pipes business and Tata Steel Colors stake to APL Apollo for ~Rs 28,000 cr while buying 52.38% of APL Apollo for ~Rs 32,300 cr
European Commission imposes definitive 9.5% anti-dumping duty on Indian cold-rolled flat steel
